precepts.text: Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? Because we will study, we will get certain instructions, but is there a follow-up to those instructions? Sometimes we give an instruction, and do we follow up and say, did you understand what I am telling you to do? Or do you go, boy, I said do it, do it. That kid is now intimidated, afraid to do it. Are we giving the proper instructions and seeing if the person is actually ascertaining the instructions that they are given? Are they just repeating what they are seeing, trying to make it? Because you know, black people, we will buy something that has to be put together and we will dump all the pieces out, we will separate them and look at the box and put the pieces together like we see it on the box, instead of reading the instructions. Well, that is what we do with the scriptures. We will read, we will study. But are we really challenging ourselves on what is being studied? Are we asking the questions? Are we going back to say, hey, I am reading this but I do not understand any of that? And as leaders, are we giving the instructions to the people? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? We all have to be guided in the instruction that we are getting. You cannot just tell a person to go do something. We are all instructed until it becomes habit.
precepts.point: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat. This is the society that we have created. A bunch of sluggard men. They have not been instructed on what hard work is. And even yourself, how many books can you say that you have read and completed in your lifetime as an adult? And then to take it a step further, how many books have you read outside of the Bible and completed as an adult? Now put that on the kid. Are you challenging them to create a habit of starting something and finishing it?

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

precepts.why:
“A wise son heareth his father’s instruction”. When you first come in as a brother, you are still attached to the life you are coming out of; somebody has to instruct you. Acts shows it. The eunuch “Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?”

We study and we get certain instructions, but is there a follow-up? When we give an instruction, do we follow up and ask, did you understand what I'm telling you to do? Or is it, boy, I said do it, do it, until the kid is intimidated and afraid to do it? Are we checking whether the person is actually ascertaining the instructions, or just repeating what they see and trying to make it?

Black people will buy something that has to be put together, dump all the pieces out, look at the picture on the box and put it together like that instead of reading the instructions. That is what we do with the scriptures. We read and study, but are we challenging ourselves on what we study? Are we asking the questions and going back to say, I'm reading this, but I don't understand any of it? And as leaders, are we giving the instructions to the people?

“And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.” We all have to be guided in the instruction we are getting. You can't just tell a person to go do something. We are all instructed until it becomes habit, and that is how a son learns to hear his father's instruction instead of becoming the scorner who hears not rebuke.

precepts.text: The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it. This is one of my favorite verses. When the Lord blesses you there is not going to be any sorrow with it. You are going to get gains. I will use it in the way of lifting weights. When you exercise or you lift weight, the muscles are being broken down. It is an acid that releases in your body and it breaks down those muscles. But when it regroups it builds more muscle and it makes you look stronger. And when you look stronger you feel stronger and you sit up a little bit more. Shout out to the greens men and the brothers that got necks. You know them brothers, they were fat and their neck sat like this, and then they start to slim down and now you can see that they have got a neck. You start to get praised, hey listen, bro, what are you doing? Something about you changed. That is what being around wise men does. And even the men that were walking with Christ, everybody knew who was walking with Christ. You sound like him. You talk like him. You have got a spirit about you that looks like Christ. It bigs you up. It makes you feel and be somebody, around wise men.
precepts.point: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise. So if you broaden that circle to wise men, meaning men that keep the commandments, then you will have righteous success.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

precepts.why:
“He that walketh with wise men shall be wise”: broaden your circle to wise men, men that keep the commandments, and you'll have righteous success. Speaking of that: “The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it.” When the Lord blesses you, there is not going to be any sorrow with it. You are going to get gains.

Think of lifting weights. When you exercise, the muscles are being broken down; an acid releases in your body and breaks them down. But when it regroups, it builds more muscle and makes you look stronger, and when you look stronger you feel stronger and sit up a little more. Shout out to the Greensmen and the brothers that got necks: they were fat and their neck sat down in their shoulders, then they slimmed down and now you can see they've got a neck. People start praising you: bro, what are you doing? Something about you changed.

That is what being around wise men does. Everybody knew the men who walked with Christ: you sound like him, you talk like him, you've got a spirit about you that looks like Christ. It bigs you up and makes you feel and be somebody.

Evil success is different. Some kids think making money on OnlyFans or social media content is success; it's not, and it's nothing to glory in. It seems good and brings profit, so it is “abomination to fools to depart from evil”. That's why rappers and entertainers keep selling digital crack and the prostitute lifestyle to the community but not to their own kids. Evil success comes with sorrow; the blessing of the Lord adds none.

precepts.text: Only by pride cometh contention: he was contending because pride was on him. I am not going to make it right with my brother; matter of fact, I have to put him to death because he is making me look bad. That is pride. But with the well advised is wisdom: let me get my spirit right; I cannot have an evil eye toward my brother.
precepts.point: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: this is the deception. He acted like his friend, talked with him over a period of time, and lured him out to the field. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with that bitter spirit; in that wrath you will slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray a brother.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Bitterness does not travel alone. Envy, pride, hatred and evil suspicion come bundled together like a cable TV package. Solomon names one: “Only by pride cometh contention”.

Cain was contending because pride was on him. Cain's attitude was: I am not going to make it right with my brother; my brother is the one who is off; in fact, I have to put him to death, because he is making me look bad. That is pride. Cain did not want to take the correction.

Then: “but with the well advised is wisdom.” The well advised are the ones who do well, like Abel. Wisdom says, let me get my spirit right; I cannot have an evil eye toward my brother. When correction comes, pride contends with it, while wisdom takes it and makes things right with the brother.

precepts.text: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children. So a good man will leave an inheritance to his what? To his children's children. What is that? That is talking about grandchildren. So if you have a good relationship with your family members and your mother and your parents, you never know. They could be saving money for your children, for their college tuition. They could be leaving that blessing for you just because of the way you conduct yourself and the way you treated them with respect. But if you are acting up and you are being disrespectful to them and you are not letting your light shine as an Israelite should, they are not going to deal with you. So you are not even going to see it. They are not going to help you with the baby when stuff comes. They are not going to help you get that stroller. They are not going to wash the kids for you. They are not going to do none of those things for you if you are not honouring and reverencing them.
precepts.point: How can the blessings of a father establish children? Let us see. But you can only get this blessing if you are honouring and respecting your parents and doing what the Lord says to do.

note.label: Honor Thy Father & Thy Mother

precepts.why:
“Honour thy father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon thee from them.” Both in word and deed means whatever you say, do it. The blessing comes from them, and “the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children.” How can the blessing of a father establish children? Solomon shows it: “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children.”

Children's children are grandchildren. So if you have a good relationship with your family, with your mother and your parents, you never know: they could be saving money for your children, for their college tuition. They could be leaving that blessing for you just because of the way you conduct yourself and the way you treated them with respect.

But you only get that blessing if you are honouring and respecting your parents and doing what the Lord says to do. If you are acting up and being disrespectful to them, and not letting your light shine as an Israelite should, they are not going to deal with you, and you will never even see it. They are not going to help you with the baby when stuff comes. They are not going to help you get that stroller. They are not going to wash the kids for you. They are not going to do none of those things if you are not honouring and reverencing them.

That is how the father's blessing establishes the houses of children: honour him in word and deed, and his inheritance reaches down to your own children.

precepts.text: Evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repayed; the Most High does not bless a man in his sins, and the trouble that keeps following is the pursuit of sin.
precepts.point: The Bible is that simple, and it destroys the confusion of the world's religions: keep the commandments and live, or break them and die. Follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes, and commandments and have life.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.” The Most High does not bless a man in his sins, and the trouble that keeps following is the pursuit of sin.

The men that followed Baal-peor were pursued by that evil until the Lord destroyed them from among the people, while those that cleaved unto the Lord were repaid with life, alive every one of them that day. It is that simple: follow after the ways of the nations and be put to death; keep the laws, statutes and commandments and have life.

precepts.text: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children.
precepts.point: The Lord grant you that ye may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband: that rest is an inheritance. The man is supposed to leave an inheritance; you are not supposed to leave your wife and your children desolate with a gang of bills. To leave an inheritance you first have to work, and you have to be wise with how you deal with your money.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Naomi prays that her daughters in law may find rest, each in the house of her husband. That rest is an inheritance, and it is what a man is supposed to leave behind. “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.”

A good man does not leave his wife and children desolate with a gang of bills; he leaves something to his children's children. Building our legacy and passing it down is one of the things we lack in Israel today, and it is important that we get back to it.

precepts.text: Evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid.
precepts.point: To be righteous is to observe to do all the commandments of the Lord; all unrighteousness is sin, and sin is the transgression of the law. David was righteous and did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while the sinner was pursued by his own evil.

note.label: 2 Samuel 17: The Counsel of the Lord Shall Stand

precepts.why:
“Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.”

When Ahithophel “saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died”. The evil counsel he devised reared its head around and bit its author. Evil pursued the sinner.

And to the righteous good was repaid. David did not want to war against his own son, yet good was repaid to him, while Ahithophel was pursued by his own evil.

precepts.text: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children, and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.
precepts.point: He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on and the innocent shall divide the silver; we do not want their Louis Vuitton, Versace, or Hermes bags, we want our kingdom back and the whole earth, because it belongs to us, plus what they took and some.

note.label: Job 27: I Will Not Remove My Integrity From Me

precepts.why:
“Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare raiment as the clay; He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on, and the innocent shall divide the silver.” Proverbs says the same: “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.”

Esau is the number one superpower and the richest people on the earth, bejeweled like no other country, able to get any Gucci, Versace, or Louis Vuitton by the snap of his finger. He may prepare it, but the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just. We do not want their Louis Vuitton, Versace, or Hermes bags; we want our kingdom back and the whole earth, because it belongs to us, plus what they took and some.

precepts.text: Evil pursueth sinners, but to the righteous good shall be repaid.
precepts.point: Many are my persecutors and mine enemies, yet do I not decline from Thy testimonies. Thy word is true from the beginning, and every one of Thy righteous judgments endureth for ever. This word was here before anything, before the Book of the Dead, before the Koran, all that other garbage.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“Evil pursueth sinners: but to the righteous good shall be repayed.” This is the reason salvation is far from the wicked: evil pursues them. They have no rest in their wicked ways and no peace, and it is the same for the wicked of our people and the wicked of the nations.

But to the righteous good shall be repaid. David has many persecutors and enemies, yet he does not decline from the testimonies; he beholds the transgressors and is grieved because they kept not the word. So he can say, “Great are thy tender mercies, O Lord: quicken me according to thy judgments.”

points: A wise son heareth his father's instruction. So a wise son is going to hear his father's instruction. And what that does in the brain, it gives that notion of how to take instructions, getting used to taking instructions from a man, to normalize it. So when you go out into society, that mutual respect that you give your father, you are going to see it in other men that are like your father. Like the ecosystem and the community that we are building here in Israel United in Christ, my son can see other men that look like me, behave like me. So therefore he is going to be more ready to take instruction from men like that. And the same goes for the sisters. But they have to be put in that environment to receive instructions.

But a scorner heareth not rebuke. And that is why some of these kids keep repeating the same habit and you keep having the same problem. It is because there is no instruction. You are just fussing at them, yelling at them, creating traumas, and they shut down. And every time they hear fussing they shut down and they regress, or they completely stop. Their confidence is not being built because they have not been put to the test to fail or succeed. All they get is, you are not doing this, you are not doing this, I asked you to do this. You have not instructed them.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: When you believe you have to just accept this life and suffer peacefully, the psychology you develop is one of hopelessness and despair. Our forefathers did not feel that way; every move they made was met with cruelty, but that still did not stop them from pushing to the point where we are born as a result of them.

Hope deferred maketh the heart sick: the heart meaning the mind. Hope is supposed to be attainable. Many of our people on the ships dove overboard because they saw no way out; they checked out mentally. But there was still a group, the elite of us, that had enough courage in the face of all that ugliness to still reproduce so that we could be here today. That took courage, faith, and hope.

When our people begin to feel that hope is out of their reach, they shortchange their own aspirations. You begin to retract into nothingness, comfortably numb with mediocrity, unproductiveness, laziness, drugs, and alcohol.

But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life. We are not looking for a nation to save us; we are looking towards the Most High, and that is where our faith is supposed to be, even in the face of virulent hatred. Why would you even fight if you do not have a victory in your mind? Because our people do not believe, they do not even fight anymore; they say just give me the bottle because I am nothing. That is a destroyed state of mind, and we cannot allow it among ourselves or our brothers and sisters. If you see our brothers and sisters carrying that kind of spirit, it is your job to find a way to pull them out of it. We are going to be our brother's and our sister's keeper; we are going to look out for each other.

The Lord put a whole generation of people to death because they was murmuring, complaining, couldn't control a mouth, gossiping and talebearing. God ain't playing with that, so we can't play with it either.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: The scriptures constantly tell you to watch your mouth. Everything you say you will give account for, so he that guards his mouth keeps his life while the one who opens his lips wide brings destruction.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: The lazy soul desires and has nothing, but the diligent soul is made fat. Desire without labor stays empty.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: The righteous man hates lying, but the wicked is loathsome and comes to shame. Righteousness keeps the upright, while wickedness overthrows the sinner.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: Some make themselves rich yet have nothing, and some make themselves poor yet have great riches. This is the man who forsakes things when he comes into the truth, giving up sponsorships and possessions, yet he still has great riches because the kingdom of heaven is coming to him.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: A man's riches may be the ransom of his life, but the poor does not even hear rebuke.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: The light of the righteous rejoices, but the lamp of the wicked is put out. Only by pride comes contention, but with the well-advised is wisdom, which points to seeking counsel at all times.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: Wealth gotten by vanity is diminished, but he that gathers by labor increases. Those chasing the fast dollar and fast money will see all those riches diminish.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: Hope deferred makes the heart sick, but when the desire comes it is a tree of life.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: Whoever despises the word is destroyed, but he that fears the commandment is rewarded. The law of the wise is a fountain of life to depart from the snares of death.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: Good understanding gives favor, but the way of transgressors is hard. Every prudent man deals with knowledge, but a fool lays his folly open for all to see.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: A wicked messenger falls into mischief, but a faithful ambassador is health.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: Poverty and shame come to the one who refuses instruction, but he that regards reproof is honored.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: He that walks with wise men shall be wise, but a companion of fools is destroyed. Every beast cleaves to its like: around fools you become a fool, around wise men you become wise.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: Evil pursues sinners, but the righteous are repaid with good. A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children, and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.

This is powerful for us as a nation. A lot of black people do not like to talk about death, but get your life insurance and leave an inheritance to your children's children. That is how far ahead we have to think.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: He that spares his rod hates his son, but he that loves him disciplines him early. Discipline your children. Esau has set it up so no one wants anyone to discipline our kids, but the discipline is a bullet.

note.label: Proverbs 13: Watch Your Mouth and Walk With the Wise

points: The righteous eats to the satisfying of his soul, but the belly of the wicked shall want.
